q: How many ecosystems live inside the Montréal Biodôme?
funFact: Each ecosystem has its own temperature, plants and animals.

q: The Biodôme building was built for the 1976 Olympics. For which sport?
funFact: It was the velodrome — a giant indoor track for racing bikes.

q: Which Biodôme animal is famous for moving very slowly?
funFact: A sloth can take a whole minute to move a few steps.

q: How many legs does every insect have?
funFact: Six legs, always — that is the insect rule.

q: How many legs does a spider have?
funFact: Eight legs means a spider is not an insect at all.

q: Butterflies can taste with which body part?
funFact: A butterfly lands on a flower and tastes it by standing on it.

q: Can penguins fly?
funFact: Penguins flap their wings to zoom through water like torpedoes.

q: Where do penguins live in the wild?
choices: The far south, not the Arctic
funFact: Penguins and polar bears never meet — they live at opposite ends.

q: Why can a sloth's fur look green?
choices: Tiny green algae grow on it
funFact: The green helps the sloth hide in the trees.

q: What is the biggest rodent in the whole world?
funFact: Capybaras live in the Biodôme's rainforest and love to swim.

q: Why does a lynx have such big fluffy paws?
choices: To walk on snow like snowshoes
funFact: Wide paws stop the lynx from sinking into deep snow.

q: The lynx belongs to which animal family?
funFact: The lynx is a wild cousin of pet cats — with pointy ear tufts.

q: What do beavers build across streams?
funFact: Beaver dams make ponds where their families stay safe.

q: What colour are a beaver's front teeth?
funFact: Iron in the teeth makes them orange — and extra strong.

q: What is a butterfly before it grows wings?
funFact: The caterpillar's whole body rebuilds itself inside the chrysalis.

q: What is the hard little case where a caterpillar transforms?
funFact: Look for chrysalises hanging like tiny lanterns at the Insectarium.

q: How do fireflies talk to each other?
funFact: Each kind of firefly has its own flashing pattern, like a secret code.

q: For its size, which animal is one of the strongest lifters?
funFact: An ant can carry many times its own body weight.

q: A puffin is a seabird that can hold what in its beak?
choices: Lots of little fish at once
funFact: A puffin can line up a whole row of fish in one beakful.

q: How do king penguins keep their egg warm?
choices: They take turns sitting in the water
funFact: The egg rests on the feet under a cozy flap of belly skin.

q: What do river otters love to do down muddy banks?
funFact: Otters slide over and over — scientists think it is just for fun.

q: What covers a porcupine's back?
funFact: A porcupine can have around 30,000 quills.

q: The golden lion tamarin is a tiny golden what?
funFact: Its fluffy golden mane is how it got the lion name.

q: What do macaws crack open with their big strong beaks?
funFact: A macaw's beak works like a nutcracker built right in.
